profile.note: Verified host baseline: DSH 0.2.1-alpha.1 (local workbench runs the @deepseek-ai/dsh-root 0.2.1-alpha.1 source tree, tag dsh-v0.2.1-alpha.1). Kernel packages are pinned to the same line as the running installation: @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools (build-against) and @deepseek-ai/schemastery (runtime). Compatibility with a running dsh is decided ONLY by peerDependencies whose name is '@deepseek-ai/dsh' or starts with '@deepseek-ai/dsh-' (packages/boot/app-boot/src/plugin-compatibility.ts), evaluated with semver.satisfies(runtime, range, {includePrerelease:true}); @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools is therefore declared as '*' in peerDependencies (a narrow range would get the plugin rejected on the next host line) while the devDependencies pin below is the build-against line used for typechecking and tests. At runtime the host's own resolution answers a linked importer's declared peers from the running installation (packages/boot/app-boot/src/profile-resolution/resolver.ts), so the plugin executes against the host's kernel copies.

knownIssues.summary: Two schemastery copies in one program break the `z<Config>` annotation
knownIssues.detail: @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools pins its own schemastery range (0.2.1-alpha.1 -> ~3.18.5-alpha.1). If the plugin's own copy is a different version (e.g. 3.18.2), the program contains two Schema types and `export const Config: z<Config> = z.object({...})` fails with TS2322 on `meta.default`.
knownIssues.resolution: Keep the @deepseek-ai/schemastery version equal to the one the pinned @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools depends on (today 3.18.5-alpha.1) and re-run pnpm typecheck after any host-line bump.

knownIssues.summary: A narrow @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools peer range makes the host refuse the plugin
knownIssues.detail: The host skips a bundle whose @deepseek-ai/dsh-* peer ranges do not satisfy the running dsh version ('is incompatible with dsh <version>'), and it never consults dependencies. package.json peerDependencies['@deepseek-ai/dsh-tools'] must therefore stay '*' (the toolchain gate enforces it).
knownIssues.resolution: Never narrow the dsh peer range; express the build-against line in devDependencies + this manifest instead, and run pnpm verify:host-compat after a host update.
